intro: Searching for a menopause clinic near you usually means you want proper time to talk through symptoms, and a clear view of your treatment options without feeling rushed. A private GP clinic that runs a menopause clinic can assess your symptoms and discuss options such as HRT. iComply can introduce you to a suitable UK professional who quotes you directly, with prices on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a menopause clinic near me usually need
need_lead: Most people typing this search want a local appointment where their perimenopause or menopause symptoms are taken seriously and explored properly.
needs: You have been putting up with hot flushes, disturbed sleep or mood changes and want to understand whether they are linked to the menopause.
Your periods have become irregular or your symptoms are changing and you would like a proper assessment rather than a quick conversation.
You want to talk through HRT options, including the different types and how they might suit you.
You are unsure whether your symptoms are menopause-related or something else, and want a clinician to consider the whole picture.
You would like a longer appointment than a standard GP slot allows, so you can cover everything without watching the clock.
context: Every doctor practising in the UK must be registered and hold a licence to practise with the General Medical Council, and GPs also appear on the GMC's GP register. You can search the GMC's online register by name before you book. Private clinics providing regulated healthcare in England must register with the Care Quality Commission, which inspects and publishes ratings; in Wales the regulator is Healthcare Inspectorate Wales, in Scotland Healthcare Improvement Scotland, and in Northern Ireland the RQIA.

It is also worth asking whether the clinician has British Menopause Society accreditation, as this shows a specific focus on menopause care. A private GP does not replace your NHS GP, and a good clinic will ask for consent to share consultation notes with your NHS practice so your records stay complete and any medication is prescribed safely.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe your main symptoms, such as hot flushes, night sweats, sleep problems, mood changes or brain fog, and how they affect daily life.
Say where you are in your menstrual history, for example whether your periods are still regular, irregular or have stopped.
Mention whether you are already taking HRT or any other medication, and whether you have tried anything before.
Explain whether you have any relevant health history, such as previous cancers, blood clots or liver problems, as this affects treatment choices.
Say roughly where you are looking for a clinic, since you searched for one near you, and whether you can travel a little further for the right appointment.
Note any preferences, such as wanting a female clinician or an appointment outside working hours if that matters to you.
questions: Do you hold British Menopause Society accreditation, and what does your menopause clinic involve?
How long is the appointment, and will there be time to go through all of my symptoms?
How do you decide whether HRT is suitable for me, and which types would you consider?
Will you share your consultation notes with my NHS GP, and how does that work?
Can HRT be continued through my NHS GP after the private consultation?
What should I do if my symptoms change before my next appointment?

faqs.q: Do I need a referral to book a menopause clinic appointment?
faqs.a: Private GP clinics that run menopause clinics usually let you book directly without a referral from your NHS GP. It is still helpful to bring any relevant history, such as recent test results or a list of your medication, to the appointment.

faqs.q: How should I prepare for a menopause appointment?
faqs.a: Tracking your symptoms for a few weeks beforehand, noting what you experience and when, gives the clinician a much clearer picture. It also helps to write down your questions and any treatments you have already tried.

faqs.q: Can I keep seeing my NHS GP as well?
faqs.a: Yes. A private GP does not replace your NHS GP, and the two can work alongside each other. A good clinic will ask for your consent to share notes with your NHS practice so your records stay complete and any prescriptions are handled safely.

faqs.q: How do I check that a clinic is properly registered?
faqs.a: You can look up the doctor by name on the General Medical Council's online register to confirm they are registered and licensed to practise. Private clinics providing regulated healthcare in England must also register with the Care Quality Commission, which publishes inspection ratings, and equivalent regulators apply in Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.

extra_heading: Choosing between a menopause clinic and a general private GP
extra: Searching for a menopause clinic near me suggests you want menopause care specifically, rather than a general private appointment where the subject might only come up briefly. A clinic that focuses on perimenopause and menopause will usually structure the consultation around your symptom history, your menstrual pattern and the treatment choices open to you, including HRT.

It helps to compare clinics on what the appointment actually covers rather than on distance alone. Ask how long the first consultation lasts, whether a follow-up is included, and whether the clinician has British Menopause Society accreditation, which indicates a particular focus on this area of care. These details tell you more about the quality of the appointment than a clinic's location or appearance.

If several clinics are within reach, it can be worth asking each one the same questions and comparing the answers before you decide. Price on application means you will need to ask directly about fees, so you can weigh up what each clinic offers alongside the cost. Your NHS GP remains your main point of contact for general care, and a private clinic should work alongside them rather than instead of them.

extra_faqs.q: Is a menopause clinic different from seeing a private GP?
extra_faqs.a: A menopause clinic is usually a private GP service with a particular focus on perimenopause and menopause, so the appointment is built around assessing your symptoms and discussing treatment options such as HRT. A general private GP appointment can cover the same ground, but may be shorter or less specialised. It is worth asking how the clinic structures its menopause appointments before you book.

extra_faqs.q: What happens at a first menopause clinic appointment?
extra_faqs.a: The clinician will usually take a full history of your symptoms, your periods and any relevant health background, then talk through options such as HRT and what might suit you. Bringing a symptom diary and a list of your current medication helps the appointment go smoothly. You can also ask about sharing notes with your NHS GP so your records stay joined up.
